record.title: GestureFAR reports real-time continuous-latent streaming gestures on BEAT2
record.summary: A September 18 preprint proposes token-causal co-speech gesture generation using continuous motion latents and a flow-matching head, then distills only that head to one step while freezing the causal backbone. On BEAT2, the authors report a 3.08 FGD one-step student at 9.3 ms/token, compared with 3.17 at 24.4 ms/token for their eight-step teacher, and 0.246 real-time factor on a MacBook Air. These are author-reported results for a specialized avatar/embodied-agent benchmark; no independent reproduction or deployment transfer is established.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that GestureFAR’s one-step student achieves 3.08 FGD and 9.3 ms/token on BEAT2, compared with 3.17 FGD and 24.4 ms/token for their eight-step teacher.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report 0.246 real-time factor on a MacBook Air for the one-step student, described as about 4.1 times real time.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The cited evaluation is on BEAT2 co-speech gesture generation; no independent reproduction or evidence of transfer to deployed heterogeneous embodied agents is established here.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the BEAT2 quality or latency results was performed; the linked project page could not be accessed.
No evidence establishes that BEAT2 results transfer to other gesture datasets, deployed avatar systems or more general embodied-agent tasks.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported BEAT2 results reproduce, continuous-latent causal generation at real-time speed on a MacBook Air changes design choices for interactive avatar systems, but remains a specialized modality and benchmark result.
limitations: Author-reported paper results; no independent reproduction.
Evaluation is specialized to BEAT2 co-speech gesture generation.
Project page was inaccessible; reported hardware generation and deployment configuration need clarification.
A favorable benchmark comparison does not establish end-to-end user benefit or broader embodied-agent capability.
brief.summary: A September 18 preprint proposes token-causal co-speech gesture generation using continuous motion latents and a flow-matching head, then distills only that head to one step while freezing the causal backbone. On BEAT2, the authors report a 3.08 FGD one-step student at 9.3 ms/token, compared with 3.17 at 24.4 ms/token for their eight-step teacher, and 0.246 real-time factor on a MacBook Air. These are author-reported results for a specialized avatar/embodied-agent benchmark; no independent reproduction or deployment transfer is established.

technical.claimed_result: On BEAT2, the authors report a one-step student at 3.08 FGD and 9.3 ms/token, an eight-step teacher at 3.17 FGD and 24.4 ms/token, and MacBook Air real-time factor 0.246.
technical.compute_or_cost: One-step student 9.3 ms/token versus 24.4 ms/token for the eight-step teacher; reported MacBook Air RTF 0.246 (~4.1x real time).
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint provides a token-causal architecture, implementation description and BEAT2 comparison tables; the experimental outcomes remain author-reported and were not independently rerun in this activation.
technical.implementation_status: Research preprint; linked project page was inaccessible during review, and no independent code-based reproduction was obtained.
technical.mechanism: A causal motion VAE produces continuous latents; a causal audio-motion transformer conditions each next latent on past motion and currently available speech; a per-token flow head samples the latent. Head-only distillation freezes the backbone and reduces the multi-step teacher flow sampler to one network evaluation.
technical.regime: BEAT2 speaker-2 test split under the cited full-body co-speech gesture protocol; 25 speakers and 1,762 clips overall. The reported runtime is on a MacBook Air; the paper text inspected does not identify the hardware generation.
technical.reproducibility: Paper gives architecture and implementation details, but code/artifact access and independent reproduction remain unresolved.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares streaming-capable MIBURI (reported 8.06 FGD, 62.9 ms/token) and LiveGesture (4.57 FGD; runtime not listed), plus an eight-step GestureFAR teacher; datasets/protocol alignment follows the paper’s stated BEAT2 comparison protocol.

brief.title: GestureFAR reports real-time continuous-latent streaming gestures on BEAT2
brief.why_it_matters: If reproduced, the result shows a practical way to combine continuous motion quality with strict online generation on consumer hardware, informing latency and representation choices for interactive avatars. Its scope is BEAT2 co-speech gesture generation; it does not establish a broadly capable embodied agent.
